scope: offline only: no ComfyUI, no checkpoint, no server. One nn.Module with the LTX block shapes (6 attentions, 2 feed-forwards, ada tables, 737.5 MB BF16 state) executed 48 times per step, which matches one sampler step reading 48 x ~773 MB from VRAM. Random weights: this measures time and eager-vs-replay identity, not model outputs.

trap.symptom: torch.xpu.graph caches ONE class-level default_capture_stream, created lazily and bound to whichever device was current at first use. Capturing on a second device with it records an EMPTY graph and only emits a UserWarning.
trap.fix: pass an explicit stream=torch.xpu.Stream(device=dev) per device, run under -W error::UserWarning, and prove non-emptiness by perturbing the static input and requiring the replayed output to move

limitations: synthetic block: same shapes and operation mix as the checkpoint, not the checkpoint code
text-context length 128 assumed for cross-attention; the real conditioning length differs
no ComfyUI patcher, routing wrapper or sampler overhead is included, so the real eager baseline is higher (3.63 s vs a 2.80 s projection) and the real gain is not yet established
capture-safety of the real block forward (host syncs, custom ops, masks) is unverified
no speed result is promoted; this validates a mechanism only
conclusion: XPU graph capture works on B70, is bit-identical to eager under deterministic mode, works across the two-device shard, and per-block capture costs only 7.4 us per replay -- so the existing set_model_patch_replace block hook is a sufficient integration point.
